      y <- lm( sales ~ oos + trend + lagsales ,data= DataPrep)

      x <- cochrane.orcutt(y)
      b <-x$coefficients[2]

      a <- x$rho

      CoefCochIncpt    <- x$Cochrane.Orcutt$coefficients[1]
      CoefCochoos      <- x$Cochrane.Orcutt$coefficients[2]
      CoefCochtrend    <- x$Cochrane.Orcutt$coefficients[3]
      CoefCochlagsales <- x$Cochrane.Orcutt$coefficients[4]

      CoefCochoos
      CoefCochtrend
      CoefCochlagsales

Hi,

we are currently working on a build service for R packages. The 'orcutt' package is building, but the tests/examples are failing due to a known issue which we hope to have fixed after the weekend. This is why Renjin can not find the package.

For now, you can simply copy the function cochrane.orcutt (only 41 lines of R code in the R package) into your own script before you call the function.

Maarten-Jan

messages.body_plain:
Hi, All

Do you have any plan to support Rejin cluster wide/multithreading ?
Is it possible to make Rejin multithread support ?
messages.body_snippet:
Hi, All

Do you have any plan to support Rejin cluster wide/multithreading ?
Is it possible to make Rejin multithread support ?

messages.subject: Re: Rejin cluster wide/multithreading support
messages.body_plain:
Yes! definitely.

Right now, Renjin is already doing some implicit paralellization, and we will likely add an inprocess, multithreaded forEach implementation in the near future.

As far as cluster wide computations, we currently use Renjin and the App Engine Pipeline library to run models on "backends" of up to 50 nodes. At some point I will open source an example of this because it works quite well but I just haven't had time.

There's lots of options for cluster computing - both Hadoop and Sparq run on the JVM, so deploying a Renjin script + jars is straightforward, but ideally you'd have a nice package that allows you to do all of that with a single line in R. Good project if anyone's interested!

Alex
